NorthstarHQ.name: Northstar
NorthstarHQ.bio: Deterministic simulation. Atlas 1.0 is out. Status: http://status.northstar.example/

alicechen.name: Alice Chen
alicechen.bio: Systems @ Northstar. Determinism maximalist. I own the renderer, so the flicker is my fault.

bmartinez.name: Bob Martinez
bmartinez.bio: Testing and CI at Northstar. If it passes on your machine I want to know which one.

carolnk.name: Carol Nakamura
carolnk.bio: Engineering manager at Northstar. Shipped Atlas. Mostly I say no to good ideas.

praman.name: Priya Raman
praman.bio: Rust internals, allocator archaeology, unreasonable benchmarks. Answers questions on Stack Overflow.

tweber.name: Tom Weber
tweber.bio: Senior editor, The Verge. Tips welcome, embargoes respected.

p-1101.author: alicechen
p-1101.text: Determinism is mostly a list of things you are no longer allowed to do, and then two years of finding out how many of them you were doing.

p-1102.author: praman
p-1102.text: Answering a question about hash map iteration order for the fourth time this year. The order is not a promise. It has never been a promise.

p-1103.author: NorthstarHQ
p-1103.text: We had 12 minutes of elevated API latency this morning starting 09:14. Everything is back. Timeline and what we are changing: http://status.northstar.example/

p-1104.author: bmartinez
p-1104.text: The postmortem reproduced from a checkpoint before anyone had finished writing the timeline. That is the entire argument for determinism in one incident.

p-1105.author: bmartinez
p-1105.text: Wrote up the flaky test that ate my month, including the nine line fix: http://bmartinez.net/posts/hash-order-bit-me

p-1106.author: praman
p-1106.text: This is the bug I answered on Stack Overflow in February: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/t-4411 - it is always iteration order, and it is always only on one CI runner.

p-1107.author: alicechen
p-1107.text: Atlas 1.0 is out. Two years of taking things away from ourselves. Full walkthrough: http://youtube.com/watch?v=atlas-walkthrough

p-1108.author: NorthstarHQ
p-1108.text: Atlas 1.0 is live. Launch notes from the team: http://eng.northstar.example/posts/shipping-atlas

p-1109.author: carolnk
p-1109.text: Shipping Atlas was three people saying no to good ideas for eighteen months. I am extremely proud of this team and I would like to sleep now.

p-1110.author: tweber
p-1110.text: New from me: Northstar's Atlas bets everything on determinism. A startup that treats an unreproducible run as a bug report. http://theverge.com/2026/atlas-determinism

p-1111.author: NorthstarHQ
p-1111.text: Fair and accurate, which is not the usual outcome. Thank you @tweber.

p-1112.author: alicechen
p-1112.text: The nine line fix that took three weeks to find is the true part of this piece. Everything else was easier than that.

p-1113.author: carolnk
p-1113.text: It does not make the software correct. It makes the incorrect parts stay still long enough to look at. I stand by my quote.

p-1114.author: alicechen
p-1114.text: Wrote down what shipping Atlas actually taught me, including the bug we allowed to exist on purpose: http://alicechen.dev/posts/what-i-learned-shipping-atlas

p-1115.author: tweber
p-1115.text: The section on the bug that was allowed to exist is the best thing I have read this month.

p-1116.author: bmartinez
p-1116.text: Nine lines. Three weeks. I am putting it on a shirt.

messages.text: Alice - Tom Weber at The Verge. I am writing about Atlas 1.0 for Thursday. Any chance of a quote on why determinism is worth what it costs you?
Happy to. Short version: it does not make the software correct, it makes the incorrect parts stay still long enough to look at. Carol said it first, so quote her for that one.
Perfect. Using both. I will send the link when it is up.
